headers.name: X-Gateway-Error
headers.writer: src/proxy/mod.rs:39460 (H1/H2 backend-response builder); src/proxy/mod.rs:47195 (build_response_with_gateway_error: overload/config_stale); src/proxy/mod.rs:272-294 (circuit-breaker/overload/config-stale reject maps, lowercase x-gateway-error); src/proxy/mod.rs:24804 restore_authoritative_gateway_error_header; src/proxy/mod.rs:24836 insert_x_gateway_error_for_backend_failure (H3: src/http3/server.rs:10506,16173; src/http3/cross_protocol.rs:10014); src/plugins/adaptive_concurrency.rs:26
headers.semantics: Closed 7-token vocabulary (src/retry.rs:212-238): connection_failure, backend_timeout, backend_error, circuit_breaker_open, overload, config_stale, concurrency_limit. On backend-dispatch responses derived only from (connection_error, final status): connection_error -> connection_failure; status 504 -> backend_timeout; status >=500 -> backend_error; else absent (src/retry.rs:281). overload is also forced on the response-transformer output-ceiling 502 (src/proxy/mod.rs:24790). Never on 2xx/3xx/4xx from the gateway core; never on native-gRPC trailers-only siblings of the overload/config_stale fences.
headers.spoofing_notes: Partially protected. Backend copies are stripped and replaced on the plain HTTP-family backend-response builders (H1/H2 src/proxy/mod.rs:39449; H3 via src/proxy/mod.rs:24827 apply_authoritative_backend_gateway_error_header). No strip was found on the native gRPC response builders (buffered src/proxy/mod.rs:36800-36840 passes backend headers through sanitize_client_response_headers_for_wire, which only removes hop-by-hop/framing fields), so a gRPC backend can inject X-Gateway-Error. NOT stripped from plugin reject header maps (only the adaptive_concurrency and CB/transformer paths restore it authoritatively), so an operator/custom plugin or reject-path header decorator can emit any value on a gateway rejection. Any non-Ferrum endpoint can send it.

headers.name: X-Gateway-Upstream-Status
headers.writer: src/proxy/mod.rs:39464 (builder .header append when upstream_is_fallback); src/http3/server.rs:10326-10327 (H3: retain+insert only when is_fallback)
headers.semantics: Only value 'degraded': load balancer used the all-unhealthy (or unhealthy-subset -> parent) fallback. May accompany any status including 2xx.
headers.spoofing_notes: H1/H2 builder path does not strip a backend-supplied X-Gateway-Upstream-Status when the gateway did not use fallback, and appends a second line when it did (no retain before .header()). H3 only strips it when is_fallback.

headers.name: gateway-error-reason
headers.semantics: Undocumented gateway-authored reason on some DispatchPolicyRejected 502s. Values seen: 'backend_tls_sni_requires_direct_h2', 'backend-egress-policy-denied' (H3 bridge only), mesh reasons such as 'mesh transport dispatch required for this backend target', 'Unix socket retry dispatch is unavailable', 'HBONE transport or gateway identity is unavailable for retry target'.
headers.spoofing_notes: Not in any strip list (src/proxy/headers.rs:745 is_backend_response_strip_header).

headers.name: Via
headers.writer: src/proxy/mod.rs:39517 (backend-response builder); values built at src/proxy/mod.rs:9373-9381 from FERRUM_ADD_VIA_HEADER (default true, src/config/env_config.rs:4788) and FERRUM_VIA_PSEUDONYM (default 'ferrum-edge', :4789); H3 src/http3/server.rs:10319
headers.semantics: '1.1 ferrum-edge' / '2.0 ferrum-edge' / '3.0 ferrum-edge' (protocol of the upstream response). Written on responses that pass through the backend-response builder, including gateway-synthesized 502/504 backend failures (buffered => '1.1 <pseudonym>'); NOT written on pre-dispatch gateway rejections built by build_response / build_response_from_normalized_reject (404, 401, 405, 431, 503 overload/config_stale, CB 503). Backend Via hops are retained and the gateway hop appended.
headers.spoofing_notes: A backend can send 'Via: 1.1 ferrum-edge' itself; operators can rename or disable it.

headers.name: Alt-Svc
headers.writer: src/proxy/mod.rs:39470 (value built at :9366 'h3=":<FERRUM_PROXY_HTTPS_PORT>"; ma=86400' when HTTP/3 enabled)
headers.semantics: Advertises HTTP/3 on backend-path responses when enable_http3.
headers.spoofing_notes: Backend alt-svc is not stripped; gateway value is appended.

headers.name: Allow
headers.semantics: Route 405: route allowed_methods uppercased, ', '-joined, config order. Protocol 405: 'GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS'.
headers.spoofing_notes: Only on gateway-built 405s; policy cannot alter it. A backend's own 405 Allow passes through untouched.

headers.name: Connection: close
headers.writer: src/proxy/mod.rs:39510 (drain / keepalive pressure / RED shedding on any response); src/proxy/mod.rs:29867 (framing observer 400); src/proxy/h1_framing_guard.rs:71-73 (parse envelopes)
headers.semantics: HTTP/1.1 only. On ordinary responses indicates gateway drain or overload pressure (probabilistic under RED), not an error.
headers.spoofing_notes: Hop-by-hop; backend Connection header is stripped (src/proxy/headers.rs:745) so a close seen by the client comes from the gateway or an intermediary.

headers.semantics: Only when the adaptive_concurrency plugin has expose_headers enabled and a TargetLimit rejection occurs.
headers.spoofing_notes: Plain names, not stripped from backend responses.

headers.name: WWW-Authenticate
headers.writer: src/plugins/utils/auth_flow.rs:657 reject() (401 + mechanism challenge); src/proxy/mod.rs:28989 missing_authentication_reject (fallback value); src/plugins/basic_auth.rs:225; src/plugins/ldap_auth.rs:91; src/plugins/oauth2_introspection.rs:1321
headers.semantics: On 401 only. Values seen: 'Basic realm="ferrum-edge", charset="UTF-8"' (basic_auth, ldap_auth), 'Bearer' (oauth2_introspection), and the literal fallback 'ferrum-edge' when no credential was presented and no applicable mechanism advertises a challenge (body {"error":"Authentication required"}). headers.name: x-request-id (request id)
headers.semantics: No request-id header is emitted by the gateway core. Only when the correlation_id plugin is enabled on the route: header x-request-id by default (configurable header_name), echoed on responses including plugin rejections by default. Accepts an incoming value from the client if present (not audited in detail).

headers.name: Content-Type: application/json
headers.semantics: All gateway JSON errors use {"error":"..."} bodies (some add "limit" or "message"). Not a Ferrum identifier by itself.

headers.name: grpc-status / grpc-message (gateway-generated)
headers.semantics: Trailers-Only HTTP 200, content-type application/grpc, empty body. HTTP reject status mapped by src/proxy/grpc_proxy.rs:2225.

headers.name: Server
headers.semantics: Ferrum sets no Server header (no writer found in src/proxy or src/http3); a Server header seen by the client is the backend's or an intermediary's.

headers.semantics: X-Ferrum-* names in the source are admin-API (e.g. X-Ferrum-Namespace-Unserved, src/admin/mod.rs:2361), internal plugin handoff markers stripped before the wire (x-ferrum-original-content-encoding, grpc-web bridge markers), or mesh request markers. outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge temporarily lacked gateway memory budget to buffer this response; the backend answered but its response was not delivered.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend is unhealthy or returned 503 (despite X-Gateway-Error: backend_error), or that retrying elsewhere helps immediately.

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge temporarily lacked gateway memory budget to buffer this request body; the request was not sent upstream.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the request body is too large or that the backend is at fault.
outcomes.remediation: Retry later; gateway operator: review request buffering budget and plugins that force buffering (WAF, validators, retries).
outcomes.notes: X-Gateway-Error is path-dependent: absent when built by build_request_buffer_capacity_response (pre-dispatch builder), but 'backend_error' when the same refusal returns through the backend-dispatch seam (request_buffer_capacity_backend_response).

outcomes.condition: Aggregate request-decode (decompression inspection) budget cannot admit the working set for a governed request.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge temporarily lacked capacity to inspect (decode) this request body; the request was not sent upstream.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the request is malformed or the backend is at fault.
outcomes.remediation: Retry later; gateway operator: review request decode budget.
outcomes.notes: Emitted as a plugin-style reject; X-Gateway-Error presence not confirmed per path.

outcomes.condition: reqwest (HTTP/1.1) lane: DestinationRule connectionPool.tcp.maxConnections reached for the destination; no socket opened.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused to open another connection to this upstream because a gateway-configured connection ceiling is reached; the request was not sent.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend is down or returned 503 (despite backend_error).
outcomes.remediation: Retry later; gateway operator: review maxConnections for this destination.
outcomes.notes: Same condition on direct-H2/H3/gRPC pools surfaces as 502 'Backend unavailable' + connection_failure (upstream.connection_limit.pooled). WebSocket upgrade path uses the same 503 body (mod.rs:14769).

outcomes.condition: DestinationRule connectionPool.http.http1MaxPendingRequests reached for the backend (upstream overflow) on the reqwest lane.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge shed this request because a gateway-configured in-flight request limit for the upstream is reached; the request was not sent.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend returned 503 or is unhealthy.
outcomes.remediation: Retry later with backoff; gateway operator: review http1MaxPendingRequests.
outcomes.notes: Carries backend_error although no backend was contacted.

outcomes.condition: Literal-IP backend (or dns_override) blocked by the backend egress policy; no dial.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused to contact the configured backend address because gateway egress policy blocks it.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend returned an error or is down.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway operator: fix the backend address or egress allow/deny policy.
outcomes.notes: H3 cross-protocol bridge additionally sets gateway-error-reason: backend-egress-policy-denied (src/http3/cross_protocol.rs:1618).

outcomes.condition: reqwest dispatch where proxy dns_override conflicts with a literal-IP backend URL host.

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"backend DNS override cannot be applied to literal target"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused to dispatch because the route's DNS override cannot be applied to the configured literal backend address (gateway configuration issue).
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend is at fault.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway operator: correct the route's dns_override/backend host.

outcomes.condition: Backend TLS SNI override that neither the direct-H2 pool nor the reqwest dial can honor.

outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend certificate is wrong or the backend failed.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway operator: review the BackendTLSPolicy/SNI override and backend protocol.
outcomes.notes: gateway-error-reason is an undocumented gateway-authored response header; it is NOT stripped from backend responses, so it is spoofable.

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused to dispatch because the secured mesh transport required for this backend was unavailable.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend application failed.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway/mesh operator: check gateway mesh identity and transport availability.
outcomes.notes: Mesh deployments only; included for completeness. Reason strings include 'mesh transport dispatch required for this backend target', 'Unix socket retry dispatch is unavailable', 'HBONE transport or gateway identity is unavailable for retry target'.

outcomes.condition: Backend returned a complete 5xx response other than 504 (connection_error=false).
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The response was relayed by Ferrum Edge with a 5xx status that, per the gateway's coarse marker, came from or after the upstream exchange; the marker alone does not prove the backend application authored it.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the gateway failed, or (without body/provenance evidence) that the application itself produced it: several gateway-local refusals also carry backend_error.
outcomes.remediation: API owner: inspect backend logs for this request; compare body with known gateway bodies.
outcomes.notes: Backend-supplied X-Gateway-Error values are stripped and replaced on this path (mod.rs:39449).

outcomes.condition: Backend itself returned a complete 504 response (e.g. an upstream load balancer timeout).
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: A 504 was relayed through Ferrum Edge and marked backend_timeout; the marker is also applied when the backend itself answered 504, so only the body distinguishes it from the gateway's own timeout.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the gateway timed out (unless the body is exactly {"error":"Backend timeout"} from a trusted Ferrum destination).
outcomes.remediation: API owner/infra behind the gateway: check the backend's own upstream timeouts.
outcomes.notes: http_observability_error_class keys backend_timeout on status 504 alone, not on ErrorClass.

outcomes.condition: Backend returned 1xx-4xx (including its own 401/403/404/429).
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The upstream application's response was relayed; no gateway failure marker is present.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That a 401/403/404/429 came from the gateway (gateway plugin rejections use the same statuses).
outcomes.remediation: Treat as application result unless other provenance says otherwise.
outcomes.notes: Any X-Gateway-Error the backend sets is stripped on H1/H2/H3 backend-response paths.

outcomes.condition: All targets in the upstream (or selected subset) were unhealthy; the load balancer used the all-unhealthy / parent-upstream fallback. Any final status.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge reports it routed this request in degraded mode because no upstream target was considered healthy; the request itself may still have succeeded.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the request failed, or which target was used.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway operator/API owner: investigate health-check failures for the upstream.
outcomes.notes: Spoofing: on the H1/H2 builder path a backend-supplied X-Gateway-Upstream-Status is NOT stripped when the gateway did not use fallback, and when it did, the builder appends a second field line. H3 replaces it only when is_fallback. Treat as spoofable.

outcomes.condition: Data-plane mode: last applied CP snapshot older than FERRUM_DP_CONFIG_MAX_STALE_SECONDS (default 3600) with CP authority lost and FERRUM_DP_CONFIG_STALE_ACTION=fail_closed (default).

public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete response. Native gRPC: HTTP 200 trailers-only grpc-status 14 grpc-message 'Gateway configuration stale' WITHOUT X-Gateway-Error. TCP/UDP listeners: accepted socket dropped / datagram session refused (no payload).

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused new work because its data plane has not received a fresh configuration from its control plane within the allowed window; the request was not sent upstream.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the client payload, credentials, or the backend are at fault.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway operator: restore control-plane connectivity / config sync; client can retry later (not dispatched).
outcomes.notes: Runs before routing, plugins and overload admission. Already-accepted connections drain. Readiness also degrades (/health ready:false).

outcomes.condition: Overload manager critical request pressure (FERRUM_MAX_REQUESTS with FERRUM_OVERLOAD_REQ_CRITICAL_THRESHOLD default 0.95) OR shutdown drain started (SIGTERM).

public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete response. Native gRPC: HTTP 200 trailers-only grpc-status 14 'Service overloaded' without X-Gateway-Error.

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused to admit this request because the gateway process is shedding load or is draining for shutdown; no upstream was contacted for this request.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend is unhealthy, that it is CPU overload specifically, or which of overload vs shutdown drain applied.
outcomes.remediation: Retry later with backoff (safe: request was not dispatched); gateway operator should check overload manager pressure and deployment/shutdown activity.
outcomes.notes: Drain and overload produce byte-identical responses; drain/pressure additionally add 'connection: close' to other responses (mod.rs:39490-39510). FERRUM_MAX_REQUESTS defaults to 0 (request-based shedding off).

outcomes.condition: Critical connection pressure (reject_new_connections) or the listener connection semaphore (FERRUM_MAX_CONNECTIONS, default 100000) exhausted; for TCP listeners also the stale-config fence.

public_signal.transport: accepted TCP socket dropped immediately before TLS/HTTP (code comment says 'TCP RST'; kernel may emit FIN or RST)

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The connection to the gateway endpoint was closed before any TLS or HTTP response; this is consistent with gateway connection admission (overload, connection limit, stale config for L4) but also with any network middlebox or a non-listening service.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That Ferrum refused it (no Ferrum marker is possible here), or any HTTP status.
outcomes.remediation: Retry with backoff; compare with a direct health check; gateway operator can check reject/connection-limit counters.
outcomes.notes: No HTTP response possible. H3 equivalent: QUIC Incoming.refuse() (src/http3/server.rs:1146).

outcomes.condition: Circuit breaker for the proxy/target is open (or half-open probe slot taken).

public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete response. Native gRPC: normalized to trailers-only grpc-status 14 (503->UNAVAILABLE) with grpc-message 'Service temporarily unavailable (circuit breaker open)'; x-gateway-error header is restored into the reject header map so it is expected on gRPC too (not lab-verified).

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected this attempt at its circuit breaker because recent failures to this upstream exceeded the configured threshold; this attempt was not sent upstream.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That no earlier retry attempt in the same request reached a backend, or that the backend is still failing now.
outcomes.remediation: Wait for the breaker cooldown and retry; API owner/gateway operator: investigate the upstream's recent failures.
outcomes.notes: Runs through after_proxy reject hooks (headers may be decorated) then the token is restored authoritatively. rejection_phase=circuit_breaker_open in logs.

outcomes.condition: FERRUM_MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_PER_IP (default 0 = off) exceeded for the resolved client IP.

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"Too many concurrent requests from this IP"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge limited this request because too many requests from the same client IP were in flight at once.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That an API rate-limit quota (rate_limiting plugin) was exhausted.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: reduce concurrency from this IP; no Retry-After is provided.
outcomes.notes: Pre-routing; no plugins run; no Retry-After / rate-limit headers; gRPC not specially mapped here (plain JSON).

outcomes.condition: Connection authenticated with a client certificate whose trust decision was withdrawn by an accepted client-CA/CRL reload (issue #3857).

public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete response; gRPC: trailers-only grpc-status 16 'Client certificate trust withdrawn'

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge no longer trusts the client certificate this connection was established with; new requests on it are refused.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the API credential/token is wrong.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: reconnect with a currently trusted client certificate; operator: check client CA/CRL changes.

public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete response; gRPC: trailers-only grpc-status 14

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge refused to process this request as TLS 0-RTT early data; resend it after the handshake completes.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the method is unsupported by the API.
outcomes.remediation: Caller/CDN: retry without early data.

outcomes.condition: No proxy route matched the request host/path.

public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete response; gRPC: trailers-only grpc-status 12 grpc-message 'Not Found'

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The endpoint answered 404 with Ferrum's route-miss body shape; if the destination is a trusted Ferrum gateway this means no gateway route matched this host/path.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That every 404 is a gateway route miss (backends can return the same bytes), or that the resource does not exist in the API.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: check host, path prefix and scheme against the published API; gateway operator: check route configuration.
outcomes.notes: Pre-plugin: no auth/CORS plugins run, so a browser CORS failure may mask it. No Via header on this gateway-built response.

outcomes.condition: Route matched but the method is not in the route's allowed_methods.

public_signal.transport: HTTP: complete response; gRPC: trailers-only grpc-status 12

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The route exists but does not accept this HTTP method; the Allow header lists the accepted methods.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That authentication failed or the resource is missing.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: use one of the methods in Allow.
outcomes.notes: rejection_phase=allowed_methods (logs only). Allow is gateway-authoritative (policy cannot alter it).

outcomes.condition: TRACE request, or CONNECT that is not a WebSocket extended CONNECT (and not HBONE).

other_headers.Allow: GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"TRACE method is not allowed"} | {"error":"CONNECT method is not allowed"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge blocks this HTTP method at the protocol level for all routes.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the route does not exist.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: do not use TRACE/CONNECT through the gateway.

outcomes.condition: Request with application/grpc content-type using a method other than POST.

public_signal.transport: trailers-only gRPC response (400 mapped to INVALID_ARGUMENT)

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the gRPC call because gRPC requires POST.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the service/method does not exist.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: send gRPC calls with POST.
outcomes.notes: Logged/metric status is 400.

outcomes.condition: One request header (name+value bytes) exceeds FERRUM_MAX_SINGLE_HEADER_SIZE_BYTES (default 16384).

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"Request header '<name>' exceeds maximum size of <limit> bytes"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the request because one header is larger than the gateway allows; the body names the header.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend rejected it.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: shrink the named header (often cookies or tokens).
outcomes.notes: Header name echoed (JSON-escaped). H1 parser buffer floor is 8 KiB above which hyper itself may reject first (see frontend_parse.hyper_default_rejects).

outcomes.condition: Sum of request header bytes exceeds FERRUM_MAX_HEADER_SIZE_BYTES (default 32768).
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the request because its headers are larger in total than the gateway allows.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend rejected it.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: reduce header size.
outcomes.notes: On HTTP/1 a head larger than the hyper parser buffer (max(limit, 8 KiB)) is rejected by hyper before this check with hyper's own response.

outcomes.condition: Number of header fields exceeds FERRUM_MAX_HEADER_COUNT (default 100).
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the request because it has more header fields than the gateway allows.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend rejected it.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: send fewer headers.

outcomes.condition: path+query length exceeds FERRUM_MAX_URL_LENGTH_BYTES (default 8192).

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"Request URL length (<n> bytes) exceeds maximum of <limit> bytes"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the request because its URL is longer than the gateway allows.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the resource is missing.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: shorten the URL / move data into the body.

outcomes.condition: Query parameter count exceeds FERRUM_MAX_QUERY_PARAMS (default 100).
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Ferrum Edge rejected the request because it has more query parameters than the gateway allows.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the API rejected a parameter value.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: send fewer query parameters.

outcomes.condition: Request body exceeds the effective limit (FERRUM_MAX_REQUEST_BODY_SIZE_BYTES default 10485760, FERRUM_MAX_GRPC_RECV_SIZE_BYTES default 4194304 for gRPC, or a lower route/request_size_limiting limit) while buffering or by Content-Length.

outcomes.remediation: Caller: reduce the payload or use a chunked/multipart upload API; operator may review the limit.

outcomes.must_not_claim: That the backend timed out.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: check local upload throughput / proxy; operator: review request body timeout.

outcomes.condition: Native gRPC: backend connect/read timeout (backend_*_timeout_ms) before response headers.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway reports the gRPC upstream did not respond within the gateway's backend timeout (connect or read).
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the client deadline expired, or which of connect/read timed out.
outcomes.remediation: API owner: check backend latency; operator: backend timeouts.
outcomes.notes: Distinguish from client deadline ('Deadline exceeded at gateway'). Connect timeout and read timeout share this message.

outcomes.condition: Client grpc-timeout expires before a stream was acquired, during buffered upload, or while a buffered response/rejection is still uncommitted (replaces it).

public_signal.transport: trailers-only 200; any buffered backend response is discarded [grpc-message: Deadline exceeded at gateway]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The caller's own grpc-timeout budget expired at the gateway before a response was delivered.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend slowness as proven cause (the client-chosen deadline may simply be short).
outcomes.remediation: Caller: raise grpc-timeout if appropriate or reduce work.
outcomes.notes: Overrides an already-selected plugin/backend error.

outcomes.condition: Client grpc-timeout fires after response HEADERS were sent but before any response DATA.

public_signal.transport: backend HEADERS then synthesized TRAILERS frame with END_STREAM (percent-encoded message) [grpc-message: Deadline%20exceeded%20at%20gateway]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The caller's grpc-timeout expired after the backend answered with headers but before any message was delivered.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend error.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: review deadline.
outcomes.notes: Backend body dropped. gRPC-Web gets an encoded trailer DATA frame. H3 relay: trailers if 0 DATA offered else RESET_STREAM(H3_INTERNAL_ERROR) (src/http3/server.rs:14059).

outcomes.condition: Client grpc-timeout fires after response DATA was already sent.

public_signal.transport: stream reset, no trailers (H2 RST_STREAM code chosen by hyper, INTERNAL_ERROR inferred; H3 H3_INTERNAL_ERROR)

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The RPC stream was reset after messages were delivered; no terminal gRPC status was received.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Success, a specific grpc-status, or which party caused the reset.
outcomes.remediation: Treat the RPC as incomplete.
outcomes.notes: No terminal status is fabricated once DATA was sent.

outcomes.condition: Buffered backend gRPC response exceeds the max response body size.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway refused a buffered gRPC response larger than its response size limit.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend crash.
outcomes.remediation: Reduce response size or raise the limit.
outcomes.notes: H3 frontend message: 'Response payload exceeded limit' (cross_protocol.rs:7849).

outcomes.condition: Client gRPC request body exceeds FERRUM_MAX_GRPC_RECV_SIZE_BYTES (default 4194304) or route limit, detected before response headers.

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway refused the gRPC request because its payload exceeds the gateway's gRPC receive limit.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend rejection.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: send smaller messages.
outcomes.notes: Streaming overflow path forwards 'gRPC request payload size exceeds maximum' (mod.rs:34060). Overflow after response headers not traced.

outcomes.condition: Non-size error while collecting a buffered gRPC request body.

public_signal.transport: trailers-only 200 [grpc-message: Failed to read gRPC request body: {GrpcProxyError Debug}]

outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: check client stream; operator: logs.
outcomes.notes: Embeds a Rust Debug rendering; match on the prefix only.

outcomes.condition: Native gRPC: credential expiry or authenticated-stream max lifetime reached before the response head is committed.

public_signal.transport: trailers-only 200 [grpc-message: credential expired | authenticated stream lifetime reached]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway ended the gRPC call because the caller's credential (or maximum authenticated lifetime) expired while the call was in progress.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the credential was invalid at submission.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: refresh credentials.
outcomes.notes: Non-gRPC gets 401 {"error":"Unauthorized"} (auth.authorization_lifetime_expired_before_commit).

outcomes.condition: Native gRPC: credential/lifetime expiry after HEADERS but before DATA.

public_signal.transport: synthesized TRAILERS grpc-status 16 [grpc-message: credential expired | authenticated stream lifetime reached]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway ended the gRPC stream with UNAUTHENTICATED because the caller's credential or maximum authenticated lifetime expired.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend authorization failure.
outcomes.remediation: Caller: refresh credentials and reconnect.
outcomes.notes: Plain HTTP/SSE never gets trailers (see streaming.authorization_lifetime_expired_after_commit).

outcomes.condition: Native gRPC: backend stream error/reset or per-frame idle read timeout after response HEADERS were forwarded.

public_signal.transport: frontend RST_STREAM (hyper chooses the reason: inner h2 Reason if present, else INTERNAL_ERROR); no grpc-status trailers synthesized

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The RPC stream was reset after response headers; no terminal gRPC status was received, so the outcome is unknown.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Success, a specific grpc-status, or that the gateway authored the failure.
outcomes.remediation: Treat as incomplete; retry only idempotent RPCs.
outcomes.notes: A gRPC client typically reports INTERNAL or CANCELLED from its own library mapping; the missing trailer is the evidence.

outcomes.condition: Backend returns its own gRPC outcome (any grpc-status).

public_signal.transport: backend HTTP status, grpc-status, grpc-message, grpc-status-details-bin forwarded; only hop-by-hop trailer names stripped

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: A grpc-status other than those synthesized by the gateway, delivered with backend headers, is the backend's RPC outcome relayed unchanged.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the gateway authored it.
outcomes.remediation: API owner: inspect service logs.
outcomes.notes: If the backend omits grpc-status, UNKNOWN(2) is recorded in log metadata only; nothing is synthesized. Native gRPC response path adds neither X-Gateway-Error nor alt-svc.

outcomes.condition: Gateway failed to build the gRPC client response.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway failed internally while building the gRPC response.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Gateway operator: logs.
outcomes.notes: Reject-builder fallback at mod.rs:25674 uses 13 with the same message.

outcomes.condition: Mesh only: target needs a mesh transport or Unix socket the direct gRPC pool cannot dial.

public_signal.transport: trailers-only 200 [grpc-message: fixed mesh refusal messages (e.g. 'gRPC to a unix-socket backend cannot be dialed directly', 'HBONE dispatch required for this backend target: {reason}')]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway refused to dispatch this gRPC call because the required mesh transport is unavailable.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Mesh operator: transport/identity.
outcomes.notes: Mesh deployments only.

outcomes.condition: Native gRPC backend literal IP denied by the backend egress policy.

public_signal.transport: trailers-only 200 [grpc-message: backend address blocked by egress policy]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway refused to contact the configured gRPC backend address because gateway egress policy blocks it.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Operator: egress policy.

outcomes.condition: Native gRPC: a protected response representation could not be inspected.

public_signal.transport: trailers-only 200 [grpc-message: response representation could not be inspected]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway withheld the gRPC response because a gateway response policy could not inspect it.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend returned INTERNAL.
outcomes.remediation: Operator: response policy / encoding.

outcomes.condition: Pre-routing header-size (431), per-IP concurrency (429) and protocol-header (400) rejections on a gRPC request.

public_signal.body_shape: same JSON bodies as the HTTP outcomes
public_signal.transport: plain HTTP response even for gRPC clients (not trailers-only)

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway rejected the gRPC call at the HTTP layer before gRPC handling (header limits, per-IP concurrency, or protocol header rules), so the gRPC client saw a non-gRPC HTTP error.
outcomes.must_not_claim: The grpc-status the client library synthesized from the HTTP status.
outcomes.remediation: Inspect the HTTP status/body; fix headers or concurrency.
outcomes.notes: gRPC clients will apply their own HTTP-to-status mapping (typically UNAVAILABLE/INTERNAL/UNKNOWN), which hides the real cause.

outcomes.condition: gRPC over the HTTP/3 frontend: backend dispatch fails before response headers.

public_signal.transport: H3 trailers-only HEADERS(200)+FIN [grpc-message: BackendUnavailable=>14 'Service unavailable'; BackendTimeout=>4 'Backend deadline exceeded'; ClientDeadlineExceeded=>4 'Deadline exceeded at gateway'; ResourceExhausted=>8 'Request payload exceeded backend limit'; ResponseTooLarge=>8 'Response payload exceeded limit'; ResponseBufferCapacity=>8 'Response buffering capacity exceeded'; Internal=>13 'Internal gateway error'; malformed client trailers=>3 'Malformed request trailers']

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: Over HTTP/3 the gateway reports a gRPC upstream failure before response headers with the listed status/message; the backend may or may not have received the call.
outcomes.must_not_claim: The exact failed step beyond the message.
outcomes.remediation: Retry only idempotent RPCs.
outcomes.notes: Messages differ from H1/H2 ('Backend unavailable', 'Resource exhausted', Internal=>14).

outcomes.condition: Any gateway gRPC error for a gRPC-Web request; also backend responses lacking grpc-status on translated gRPC-Web.

public_signal.body_shape: gRPC-Web trailer frame (0x80 flag) carrying grpc-status/grpc-message; base64 for grpc-web-text
public_signal.transport: HTTP 200 with body-framed trailers [grpc-message: same mapping and messages as native gRPC]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: gRPC-Web errors arrive as HTTP 200 with a body-framed trailer carrying grpc-status.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Success from HTTP 200.
outcomes.remediation: Decode the trailer frame.

outcomes.condition: FERRUM_WEBSOCKET_MAX_CONNECTIONS (default 20000) or per-IP WebSocket limit reached.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway refused the WebSocket upgrade because its WebSocket connection limit (global or per client IP) is reached.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Retry later; operator: WebSocket limits.
outcomes.notes: Global and per-IP limits send identical bytes; no X-Gateway-Error.

outcomes.condition: Origin header not in the route's allowed_ws_origins.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway refused the WebSocket upgrade because the Origin is not allowed for this route.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Authentication failure.
outcomes.remediation: Use an allowed Origin or ask the operator.

outcomes.condition: Credential expiry elapsed before the WebSocket upgrade completed.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The caller's credential expired before the WebSocket upgrade completed.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Invalid credential at submission.
outcomes.remediation: Refresh credentials.

outcomes.condition: FERRUM_WEBSOCKET_MAX_LIFETIME_SECONDS (default 3600) elapsed before upgrade completed.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway's maximum WebSocket lifetime elapsed before the upgrade completed.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Retry; operator: lifetime settings.

outcomes.condition: Backend WebSocket dial fails (DNS, TCP, TLS, connect timeout) OR the backend answered the upgrade with a non-101/200 status.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway could not establish the upstream WebSocket (connect/DNS/TLS failure or the backend refused the upgrade); the backend's own response is not shown.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Which of these happened, or that the backend is down (it may have answered the upgrade with an error).
outcomes.remediation: Operator: gateway logs; API owner: backend upgrade handling.
outcomes.notes: Backend's own rejection status/body is NOT relayed; no 504 variant; no X-Gateway-Error. H3 sends {"error":"DNS resolution for backend failed"} for DNS failures.

outcomes.condition: DestinationRule maxConnections reached for the WebSocket backend.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway refused the upgrade because a gateway-configured backend connection ceiling is reached.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Retry later; operator: maxConnections.
outcomes.notes: Same body as the reqwest HTTP lane but without X-Gateway-Error.

outcomes.condition: Gateway-internal WebSocket upgrade failure.

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"Internal server error during WebSocket upgrade"} | {"error":"Invalid backend path coordinates"} | {"error":"WebSocket request buffering invariant violated"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway failed internally during the WebSocket upgrade.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Operator: logs.

outcomes.condition: Circuit breaker open or adaptive_concurrency shed on a WebSocket upgrade (overload/config_stale pre-routing fences also apply).

public_signal.body_shape: the same JSON bodies as the HTTP admission outcomes

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway refused the WebSocket upgrade at an admission fence named by X-Gateway-Error; the upgrade was not sent upstream.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Retry later.
outcomes.notes: Only these four pre-upgrade WebSocket rejects carry X-Gateway-Error.

outcomes.condition: Gateway policy close mid-session: credential expired, maximum lifetime, client trust withdrawn, fragmented-message limit (FERRUM_WEBSOCKET_MAX_INCOMPLETE_MESSAGE_FRAMES 1024 / _SECONDS 60), ws_rate_limiting, WAF message block.

public_signal.transport: Close frame sent to both peers (bounded 100 ms write), then teardown [ws close reason: "credential expired | maximum lifetime reached | client trust withdrawn | fragmented message limit | <ws_rate_limiting close_reason, default 'Frame rate exceeded'> | message rejected by security policy | message exceeds inspectable size | message could not be inspected"]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway closed the WebSocket for a policy reason given in the close reason (credential/lifetime/trust, fragment limit, rate limit, or WAF).
outcomes.must_not_claim: An application-level error, or a policy other than the stated reason.
outcomes.remediation: Act on the close reason: refresh credentials, slow down, or change message content.
outcomes.notes: The reason string distinguishes the policy. Tunnel mode (FERRUM_WEBSOCKET_TUNNEL_MODE) sends no Close frame.

outcomes.condition: Gateway drain/shutdown or idle timeout (FERRUM_WEBSOCKET_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, default 300).

public_signal.transport: Close frame to both peers [ws close reason: 'gateway draining | idle timeout']

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway closed the WebSocket because it is draining or the session was idle.
outcomes.must_not_claim: An application error.
outcomes.remediation: Reconnect; send keepalives if idle.
outcomes.notes: A relay failure racing the drain also becomes 1001 'gateway draining'.

outcomes.condition: Frame > FERRUM_MAX_WEBSOCKET_FRAME_SIZE_BYTES (default 16 MiB) or message > 4x that; or ws_message_size_limiting ceiling.

public_signal.transport: Close frame to both peers (either direction) [ws close reason: "'' (global limit) | <plugin close_reason, default 'Message too large'>"]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: A WebSocket frame or message exceeded a gateway size limit and the session was closed.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Protocol corruption, or which direction violated it without logs.
outcomes.remediation: Send smaller messages/frames.
outcomes.notes: Direction-dependent class: request_body_too_large (client->backend) or response_body_too_large (backend->client).

outcomes.condition: Transport failure on either relay half (e.g. backend TCP reset / I/O error).

public_signal.transport: Close frame written to the surviving peer [ws close reason: 'relay error']

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway closed the WebSocket because relaying to the other side failed.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Which side failed or why.
outcomes.remediation: Reconnect; operator: logs.
outcomes.notes: Does not say which side failed.

outcomes.condition: RFC 6455 protocol violation by either peer.

public_signal.transport: Close frame to both peers [ws close reason: 'protocol error']

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway closed the WebSocket with a protocol error; a peer violated RFC 6455 (or, unverified, the backend dropped TCP without a Close handshake).
outcomes.must_not_claim: Which peer misbehaved.
outcomes.remediation: Check client and backend WebSocket framing.
outcomes.notes: Inferred, unverified: a backend TCP FIN without a Close handshake may surface in tungstenite as Protocol(ResetWithoutClosingHandshake) and therefore 1002 rather than 1011.

outcomes.condition: A peer (normally the backend) sends a Close frame.

public_signal.transport: peer Close code and reason forwarded verbatim

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: A Close code not in the gateway's set (1001/1002/1008/1009/1011 with the gateway's reasons) was relayed from the backend unchanged.
outcomes.must_not_claim: That the gateway authored it.
outcomes.remediation: Interpret per the application's close codes.
outcomes.notes: If a gateway policy Close was already published, the policy Close wins.

outcomes.condition: FERRUM_WEBSOCKET_TUNNEL_MODE=true (H1/H2, no frame plugins): lifetime, drain or trust stop.

public_signal.transport: raw transport dropped without a Close frame (client libraries typically report 1006)

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The WebSocket transport ended without a Close frame.
outcomes.must_not_claim: A specific cause, or that 1006 was transmitted by a peer.
outcomes.remediation: Reconnect; operator: logs.
outcomes.notes: No size/fragment/WAF/rate closes in tunnel mode.

outcomes.condition: RFC 9220 WebSocket over HTTP/3 when FERRUM_HTTP3_WEBSOCKET_ENABLED is false.

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"WebSocket over HTTP/3 is disabled on this gateway"}

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: WebSocket over HTTP/3 is disabled on this gateway.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Use HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 WebSocket.

outcomes.condition: Gateway shutdown (HTTP/2 connections).

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The server announced graceful connection shutdown (GOAWAY NO_ERROR); streams above last-stream-id were not processed.
outcomes.must_not_claim: TLS failure or that in-flight streams failed.
outcomes.remediation: Open a new connection.
outcomes.notes: Library behaviour; FERRUM_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_SECONDS (default 30) bounds the process drain.

outcomes.condition: Authenticated stream expired and the client did not drain the terminal, or client-cert trust withdrawn for the TLS connection.

public_signal.transport: GOAWAY then TCP hard close after 2 s (AUTHORIZATION_TRANSPORT_CLOSE_SETTLE, mod.rs:14205); sibling streams can die [h2: NO_ERROR (GOAWAY, hyper)]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The server sent GOAWAY and closed the connection.
outcomes.must_not_claim: A specific cause.
outcomes.remediation: Reconnect; if repeated with long streams, check credential expiry.

outcomes.condition: Client opens more concurrent streams than advertised SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The stream was refused because the client exceeded the server's advertised concurrent stream limit; the request was not processed.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Respect SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS.
outcomes.notes: Ferrum only configures the limit.

outcomes.condition: Client triggers too many pending-accept or local-error resets (rapid reset).

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The server closed the connection for excessive stream resets.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Fix client stream reset behaviour.
outcomes.notes: Unverified library code.

outcomes.condition: reject_new_connections overload flag or listener draining (QUIC).

public_signal.transport: QUIC handshake refused [h3: QUIC transport CONNECTION_REFUSED (quinn Incoming::refuse)]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The QUIC handshake was refused by the server, consistent with gateway overload or drain.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Network blocking with certainty.
outcomes.remediation: Retry later or fall back to TCP.
outcomes.notes: Library code.

outcomes.condition: Gateway shutdown, or overload keepalive-pressure tier rising (one-shot GOAWAY per connection).

public_signal.transport: H3 GOAWAY then connection close after drain [h3: GOAWAY; later streams H3_REQUEST_REJECTED (vendored h3); on shutdown CONNECTION_CLOSE app code 0x0100 H3_NO_ERROR reason 'shutdown']

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The server announced graceful HTTP/3 shutdown or connection shedding; later streams were rejected unprocessed.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Failure of in-flight streams.
outcomes.remediation: Open a new connection.
outcomes.notes: H1/H2 instead get 'connection: close' on responses.

outcomes.condition: Client-cert trust withdrawn for the QUIC connection.

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway closed the QUIC connection because the client certificate is no longer trusted.
outcomes.must_not_claim: API credential failure.
outcomes.remediation: Reconnect with a trusted client certificate.

outcomes.condition: QUIC/TLS handshake exceeds FERRUM_FRONTEND_TLS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS.

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The QUIC/TLS handshake did not complete within the gateway's handshake timeout.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Certificate rejection.
outcomes.remediation: Check UDP path and client TLS.

outcomes.condition: HTTP/3 frontend: backend read error, size overflow, deadline after DATA, or auth expiry after DATA.

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The HTTP/3 response stream was reset after it started; the body is incomplete.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Success, or the cause.
outcomes.remediation: Treat as incomplete.
outcomes.notes: Truncation is distinguishable from EOF on H3.

outcomes.condition: Gateway answered (incl. rejects) and no longer needs the request body.

outcomes.must_not_claim: A failure.
outcomes.remediation: None.
outcomes.notes: Not an error; clients must not treat it as failure.

outcomes.condition: HTTP/3 request HEADERS not received within FERRUM_HTTP_HEADER_READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS.

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The server abandoned the HTTP/3 request stream because headers did not arrive in time.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure.
outcomes.remediation: Send headers promptly.
outcomes.notes: docs/http3.md:1460-1467.

outcomes.condition: Request field section larger than advertised SETTINGS_MAX_FIELD_SECTION_SIZE, or a non-DATA frame declaring more than 2x that.

public_signal.transport: 431 from h3 library; frame over-declaration closes the connection [h3: H3_EXCESSIVE_LOAD (0x0107) connection error for an over-declared frame length]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The request headers exceeded the HTTP/3 field-section limit.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend rejection.
outcomes.remediation: Reduce header size.
outcomes.notes: Below the h3 cap Ferrum's own 431 JSON applies.

outcomes.condition: HTTP/3 plain CONNECT or unsupported :protocol; CONNECT-UDP disabled or sent in 0-RTT.

public_signal.body_shape: {"error":"CONNECT method is not allowed"} | {"error":"CONNECT-UDP over HTTP/3 is disabled on this gateway"} | {"error":"CONNECT-UDP is not allowed in 0-RTT early data"}
public_signal.transport: H3 response or stream reset [h3: H3_MESSAGE_ERROR stream reset for an unregistered :protocol (h3 library)]

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway does not allow this CONNECT/extended CONNECT form over HTTP/3.
outcomes.must_not_claim: Route absence.
outcomes.remediation: Use a supported protocol.

outcomes.must_not_claim: Backend failure unless the body says resolution/socket failure.
outcomes.remediation: Act on the body reason.

outcomes.condition: spec_expose plugin cannot fetch the upstream spec, or is busy.
outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: The gateway's spec_expose plugin could not serve the API specification right now.
outcomes.must_not_claim: API failure.
outcomes.remediation: Retry after the indicated delay.
outcomes.notes: The only gateway-originated Retry-After found on the proxy data path; core overload/CB/concurrency/rate-limit/WS/H3 rejects send none. Fetch-failure status can vary.

outcomes.condition: Proxy has >=1 applicable auth plugin, no principal (Consumer or external identity) was committed, and no plugin produced a Reject (Multi) / every applicable plugin returned Continue (Single). Typical: no credential at all (every mechanism extracted Missing: absent header/query, foreign Authorization scheme for jwt/jwks/oauth2/basic, mtls_auth without a client cert); a jwks_auth/oauth2_introspection/oidc credential that validated but had no non-blank identity claim; a valid OIDC session lacking the identity claim; soap_ws_security identity config passing through (mixed_route, or reject_missing_security_header=false).

other_headers.WWW-Authenticate: exactly one value: first authentication_challenge() among applicable auth plugins in ascending priority -> 'Bearer' (oauth2_introspection) | 'Basic realm="ferrum-edge", charset="UTF-8"' (ldap_auth, basic_auth) | literal fallback 'ferrum-edge'
other_headers.Set-Cookie: Multi mode only: cookies staged by earlier rejecting attempts (only oidc_relying_party stages); Single mode drops them

outcomes.minimum_truthful_diagnosis: If the response came from a Ferrum Edge gateway, its (proxy auth phase) plugin produced this outcome; the condition is: Proxy has >=1 applicable auth plugin, no principal (Consumer or external identity) was committed, and no plugin produced a Reject (Multi) / every applicable plugin returned Continue (Single). Typical: no credential at all (every mechanism extracted Missing: absent header/query, foreign Authorization scheme for jwt/jwks/oauth2/basic, mtls_auth without a client cert); a jwks_auth/oauth2_introspection/oidc credential that validated but had no non-blank identity claim; a valid OIDC session lacking the identity claim; soap_ws_security identity config passing through (mixed_route, or reject_missing_security_header=false).
